rule_gaps: the Jewelry vocabulary fires on the bare metal word: 'Sølvkroken' (7 fishing-tackle rows), 'Sølvvask', 'Snorstopper … 82 Sølv' all land in Jewelry — require a jewellery noun or a jewellery crumb, not 'sølv'/'gull' alone
facetrules Jewelry `type` matches 'ring'/'rull' anywhere in the name: 'Step-Up Ring' (lens adapter), 'støvrull' (lint roller), 'skirens', 'Bennet Ring Ear' (a hoop earring) all get type Rings
'gull'/'sølv' used as a COLOUR ('Gummistøvel Gull', '82 Sølv') is read as facets.material

Mestergull's feed publishes bare category labels as product names ('Ørepynt Sølv' x11, 'Sølje Sølv' x4, 'Veskestøl', 'Ur Stål'); slugId(brand,name) then collapses a whole brand's earrings into ONE row — 33 rows here, and srcCat 'Hjem > Produkter'/'Produkter' (43 rows) carries no signal to classify or name them

brand strings are not normalised: SYLVSMIDJA/Sylvsmidja, GEORG JENSEN/Georg Jensen, EFVA ATTLING/Efva Attling, SIF JAKOBS/Sif Jakobs each split the brand filter, and 'PIA & PER' is stored HTML-escaped
shop menu crumbs and shop names arrive as brand: 'Charms' (Skoringen), 'Gaveartikler', 'MESTERGULL', 'Kid'
165 of 300 rows (55%) have no stored image — every Mestergull/Bjørklund sampled shop contributes
notes: The genuine jewellery core (Bjørklund/David-Andersen/Sylvsmidja rows) is in good shape; the damage is concentrated in two places — 33 rows that are not jewellery at all (fishing tackle, silver flatware, ski wax, a lens ring, a lip stain) pulled in by 'sølv'/'ring' matching, and 33 Mestergull feed rows whose name is a bare category label so one row stands in for a brand's whole earring range.
